title: Grace, Lapse and Reinstatement of a Circle Membership in Arrears
content:
## Grace

When a billed dues period goes unpaid past its due day the Northbeam Circle Membership drops into grace,
and where the tier suspends benefits in grace the member may not redeem points or benefit credit until
the dues are settled. A membership is put back to active from grace when the outstanding dues and the
late fee have been settled inside grace.

> The clause "The late fee of the tier is billed when grace begins, and it is owed whether or not the
> membership is later reinstated." is **no longer in force**. The late dues fee figure recorded for each
> tier remains in force as a figure of this policy.

## When a membership may be moved to lapsed

A membership may not be moved to lapsed before the grace days of its tier have run in full, counted from
the day the retailer books the dues charge for the current billing period. Grace days are counted as
calendar days with the day the dues charge is booked counting as day zero, no business-day adjustment is
made, and a period that ends on a day the stores are shut is not extended. The day the dues charge for
the current billing period was booked is read from the membership ledger, and the standing of the
membership from the record; neither is taken from the caller's account of when the bill arrived. The move
to lapsed is the step at which grace ran out with the dues still unpaid.

Because the booking day counts as day zero and the boundary day itself satisfies the period, a tier
carrying a grace period may be moved to lapsed on the day the grace days are complete, and not on the day
before.

## Reinstatement at the former tier

A lapsed membership is reinstated at its former tier only when the customer asks within the reinstatement
window of that tier, measured from the day the membership was moved to lapsed. The reinstatement window is
counted in calendar days from the lapse day itself, which counts as day zero. The lapse day and the count
of reinstatements already taken are read from the membership record before the reinstatement is taken.

Reinstatement is refused once the membership has already been reinstated as many times as the tier
allows, and after the window the customer enrols afresh at the dues then published, with the former term
dates not carried over. The reinstatement fee of the tier is billed on reinstatement, and unpaid dues
from before the lapse stay owed.

## Boundary cases on the two windows

On a tier whose reinstatement window is recorded as 60 days, a request made on the sixtieth day after the
lapse day is inside the window and one made on the sixty-first day is outside it, because the lapse day
counts as day zero and the last day of the window itself qualifies. Where the same membership has already
been reinstated as many times as its tier allows, the request is refused inside the window as well as
outside it.

superseded_clauses: The late fee of the tier is billed when grace begins, and it is owed whether or not the membership is later reinstated.
